title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of 'magasins' (stores of specimens) for a combinatorial or tame 'analysis situs'.
- M is a set of 'spécimens' X, Y, ... with two order relations.
- X ≤ Y reads 'X is a sub-specimen (face) of Y'. The notation Ỹ denotes the set of sub-specimens Y' ≤ Y.
- X ≪ Y reads roughly 'X lies in the shadow of Y'.
- L ⊂ M is the set of 'lieux' (points).
- omb(X) is the shadow of X, i.e. the points x ∈ L with x ≪ X. omb(X)° is its 'interior': the points whose minimal carrier is X itself, i.e. X̃^x = {X}.
- ∥ is a disjointness relation. The previous page lists axioms Mag 3 and Mag 4 for a relation |0| on M and the 'strictly divisible' case. There |0| on M is recovered from a relation ∥ on L via MagL2: X |0| Y if every interior point of X is disjoint from every interior point of Y.

This page.
1. It first defines the 'quasi-ensembliste' case (Magquasi): distinct points are always disjoint, i.e. ∥ = ≠ on L.
2. It then states a Proposition-Scholie: 'pré-ensembliste' magasin structures on M are exactly pairs (≤, ≪) of order relations, with nothing more, satisfying three axioms.
   - Mag 1: X ≤ Y ⇒ X ≪ Y.
   - Mag 2 (existence of carriers): for X ≪ Y, the set Ỹ^X = {Y' ≤ Y | X ≪ Y'} has a least element. This is the 'support' of X inside Y, analogous to the carrier simplex of a point in a simplicial complex.
   - Mag L1: every X has an interior point, i.e. some x ∈ L whose carrier in X is X itself.
   The disjointness data have thus been eliminated: in the pre-ensembliste case they are determined by the orders.
3. A forward reference ('CR VII p. 57') points to a counterexample. It shows that these axioms do not force M to embed into Figel(L). By the next page, a Figel(L) element is a set-theoretic figure: a family of subsets of L, closed under the needed operations.
4. 'Pour mémoire': under Mag L1 (judged an important condition here), for every figure F there is an order-isomorphism Ssfig(F) ≅ Ssfig(noyaux(F)), F' ↦ noyaux(F'). Here Ssfig means subfigures and noyaux means kernels. So a subfigure is determined by its kernel.
5. The page ends by warning that, even in the quasi-ensembliste case, one does not necessarily have the 'ensemblistic' reflection properties. These are conditions b) and c) on the next page: shadow and inclusion relations between set-theoretic realisations should reflect back to the figures.
6. The next page then characterises 'ensembliste' magasins as subsets M ⊂ Figel(L) ⊂ PP(L). The conditions are closure under taking lower sets F_{≤X} and containing all point-figures {{x}}. This is essentially a hereditary family of face-posets, i.e. an abstract cell or simplicial-complex-like structure.

Purpose: to find a minimal combinatorial axiomatics for 'figures' (cells, strata) and their incidences. This is the base of the 'ateliers de visualisation'. The aim is to decide when the abstract order-theoretic data are realised set-theoretically by point sets.
errors: The Proposition-Scholie is essentially a tautological repackaging: once ∥ is fixed to be ≠ (or determined by the orders), 'structure = (≤, ≪) satisfying Mag1, Mag2, MagL1' is close to a definition. Nothing is proved on the page.

Mag L1 is written with 'i.e.' equivalences: omb(X)° ≠ ∅ ⇔ ∃x with x ≪° X ⇔ X̃^x = {X}. This silently presupposes that Ỹ denotes the sub-specimens of Y and that 'interior' means 'carrier equals X'. That is consistent, but it is never stated on this page.

The Ssfig isomorphism is asserted without proof. Injectivity, i.e. a subfigure being determined by its kernels, plausibly needs Mag 2 (carriers) as well as Mag L1. Under Mag L1 alone it is not obviously true; the gap is unverified.
The previous page's footnote notes that antireflexivity of |0| needs omb(X)° ≠ ∅. This page makes that explicit as Mag L1, so the earlier gap is closed here.

ideas.what: Axiomatics of a 'magasin': a set of specimens with an order ≤ (face) and a coarser order ≪ (shadow/incidence), satisfying Mag1 (≤ ⊂ ≪) and Mag2 (existence of least carriers)
ideas.modern_name: Abstract cell complex / face-poset with carrier map; closest: Tucker–Kovalevsky abstract cell complexes, CW posets (Björner), cellular stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: A.W. Tucker (1933), V. Kovalevsky (1989), A. Björner (1984)
ideas.where_published: Only hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme (tame topology, 'dévissage' of stratified structures); the magasin axiomatics itself is unpublished

ideas.what: Interior-point axiom MagL1: every specimen has a point whose carrier is the specimen itself
ideas.modern_name: Nonempty open cells / every stratum has nonempty relative interior; 'carrier' of a point in a simplicial complex

ideas.what: Quasi-ensembliste case: distinct points are disjoint, and disjointness on specimens is derived from disjointness of interior points
ideas.modern_name: Partition of a space into disjoint open cells (strata); disjointness relation in mereotopology

ideas.what: Order-isomorphism between subfigures of F and subfigures of its kernels (noyaux) under MagL1
ideas.modern_name: Subcomplexes determined by their sets of open cells (cells ↔ subcomplex lattice)

ideas.what: Abstract magasins need not embed in set-theoretic figures Figel(L); a counterexample is referenced (CR VII p. 57), and set-theoretic realisability is formulated as reflection conditions
ideas.modern_name: Realisability of abstract incidence or closure structures by point sets (representation-theorem type question)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogues: Stone-type representation, realisability of posets as face posets

missed.claim: Grothendieck develops, but does not finish, a two-order axiomatics (≤ face, ≪ shadow) for combinatorial 'figures'. It comes with a disjointness relation and a realisability question: when does an abstract magasin embed into set-theoretic figures? This sits between abstract cell complexes and stratified tame topology and seems not to have been taken up as such.
missed.quote: Voir exemple dans CR VII p. 57 pour montrer que ceci n'implique pas que M se plonge dans Fig el(L)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Characterising which incidence posets with a 'shadow' order are realised by point-set figures is a natural question. It is relevant to digital topology, to combinatorial models of o-minimal or stratified spaces, and to exit-path or poset models of stratifications. The archive contains a concrete counterexample (CR VII p. 57) that is not in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished, idiosyncratic axiomatics, part of Grothendieck's late 'analysis situs' programme, and as such it is little known. The actual content on this page, however, is close to definitional or folklore combinatorial topology: carriers, interior points, subcomplexes determined by open cells. The most interesting point is the referenced non-realisability example, which is only pointed to, not given.
transcription_corrections: 'amb(X)°' should read 'omb(X)°' (ombre / shadow), consistent with the previous page.
The parenthetical after Mag L1 reads more like '(qui semble être une condition assez importante ici)' than '[?] anodine importante'.
The first line likely reads 'la relation de disjonction sur M en la restreignant à L'.
The axiom label written in the image looks like 'MagL1' with an overwritten character ('Mag L&1'). It is the same Mag L1 referred to later.
'on a pour F ∈ 𝓕' is preceded by the crossed-out fragment 'qu'on a'; the struck text should be dropped.
